Definition: from G3435; a stain; i.e. (figuratively) immorality:--filthiness.
BiblicalUsage: Molysmos is filthiness, a stain — Paul tells the Corinthians to cleanse themselves from all filthiness of the flesh and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the cleansing is a work I am told to do: God gives the promises, and I wash.
